rules.sentence: Although rare, appendiceal tumors most commonly present with clinical features of acute appendicitis.

Atypical symptoms and high-risk features, including advanced age, altered bowel habits, rectal bleeding, unexplained anemia, weight loss, and chronic abdominal discomfort, should be recognized as red flags.
Rigorous histopathologic evaluation of appendectomy specimens is essential, as approximately 50% of appendiceal tumors are identified incidentally.
Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion in patients presenting with atypical appendicitis or features suggestive of malignancy.
Optimal management of appendiceal tumors relies on coordinated interprofessional collaboration to ensure comprehensive, patient-centered care.
